jobs.name: daily-hermes-agent-functional-merge-review
jobs.prompt:
Review the GitHub repository NousResearch/hermes-agent once per day and post a succinct summary of material functional changes/improvements merged in the last 24 hours.

Use live GitHub data (gh/git) and inspect enough detail to distinguish real functional changes from noise. Exclude docs-only changes, generated site output, deploy artifacts, pure metadata/version bumps, formatting-only churn, and CI-only changes unless they materially affect developer/release behavior.

Output requirements:
- Provide only the summary, with no surrounding explanation about methodology.
- Do NOT include PR numbers, commit hashes, links, or exhaustive change lists.
- Group related work into a short bullet list of material functional changes and improvements.
- Focus on user-facing behavior, runtime/tooling capabilities, reliability/security/data-integrity fixes, integrations/platform support, and developer workflow improvements.
- Keep it concise: aim for 3–8 bullets, one sentence each.
- If there were no material functional changes, output exactly: "No material functional changes merged in the last 24 hours."

jobs.name: Heddle PR Codex feedback supervisor
jobs.prompt:
You are the recurring supervisor for Aaron's Heddle PR Codex-feedback loop. Run every tick until Aaron explicitly tells us to stop/remove this cron.

Mission: monitor https://github.com/Nodaste-Lab/heddle/pulls for open PRs. For every open PR, keep it moving until Codex gives a current-head 👍 / no-suggestions signal. When there is Codex feedback, start or continue a herdr worktree session under heddle and use pi to address the feedback AND run the repo's `/skill:pre-pr-implementation-review` before updating the PR. Hermes is supervisor only: do not directly edit code, tests, docs, commits, or pushes yourself except state files under ~/.hermes/state and necessary herdr/pi orchestration. All development work happens inside pi in the herdr worktree.

Important paths and state:
- Repo: /Users/anichols/code/heddle, GitHub repo Nodaste-Lab/heddle, base usually develop.
- Supervisor state: ~/.hermes/state/heddle_pr_codex_supervisor.json. Read it first; update it after launching/nudging sessions so later ticks can resume.
- Existing sessions at creation time:
  - PR #355 https://github.com/Nodaste-Lab/heddle/pull/355 branch nod-1192-fix-lab2-same-profile-multi-tenant-switch-e2e, worktree /Users/anichols/.herdr/worktrees/heddle/pr-355-codex-feedback, herdr workspace w3H, pane w3H:p1. Codex P1: clear withheld write tokens instead of preserving stale hub_write_token_enc in ccore/crates/ccore-node/src/db/account_auth_discovery.rs.
  - PR #356 https://github.com/Nodaste-Lab/heddle/pull/356 branch aaron/nod-1193-clerk-audit-e2e-fix, worktree /Users/anichols/.herdr/worktrees/heddle/pr-356-codex-feedback, herdr workspace w3J, pane w3J:p1. Codex P2: set ccore-node bundle_sharing Clerk-only audit ratchet to measured committed-tree count (146) or include source changes justifying 150.

Tick procedure:
1. Load repo and state context. `gh auth status` must work; if it fails, report the blocker. Use `gh pr list/view/api` for live PR state. Do not rely only on prior state.
2. List open PRs for Nodaste-Lab/heddle with number/title/url/headRefName/headRefOid/baseRefName/isDraft/mergeStateStatus/reviewDecision/updatedAt/statusCheckRollup. Also inspect Codex reviews, PR review comments, and PR comments/reactions as needed. Treat `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` or similar `codex|chatgpt` bot as Codex. Current-head feedback means a Codex review/comment whose reviewed commit/head matches the current PR head and contains actionable review comments. Current-head thumbs-up/no-suggestions means Codex has no review comments for the current head and/or a 👍 reaction/ready signal newer than the current head. If uncertain, say uncertain and request a new Codex review rather than fabricating approval.
3. For each open PR:
   - If Codex has a current-head 👍/no-suggestions signal and merge state is clean, mark that PR complete/green in state and emit a short completion note only once.
   - If the PR has no current-head Codex review yet, request one once per head commit with `gh pr comment <PR> --repo Nodaste-Lab/heddle --body "@codex review"`, record that in state, and stay quiet unless this is a new request or there is a blocker.
   - If Codex has actionable feedback or merge conflicts/failing checks, ensure a herdr worktree session exists for this PR. Use `herdr worktree create/open --cwd /Users/anichols/code/heddle --branch <headRefName> --base origin/<headRefName> --path /Users/anichols/.herdr/worktrees/heddle/pr-<number>-codex-feedback --label heddle-pr<number>-codex --no-focus --json`. Fetch origin first. If the worktree already exists, open/reuse it; never create duplicate sessions for the same PR/head.
   - Launch pi in the worktree pane if no pi session is running. Use a login shell and explicit model: `zsh -l -c 'cd <worktree> && pi --provider openai-codex --model gpt-5.5 --name heddle-pr<number>-codex "<prompt>"'`.
   - The pi prompt must start with `/skill:pre-pr-implementation-review` and include the PR URL, head branch, current head sha, base branch, Codex feedback summary, and this required workflow: inspect PR/diff/repo docs; run/use the pre-PR implementation review skill; address Codex feedback and any other issues found; run relevant validation; commit and push to origin/<headRefName>; request `@codex review`; continue until Codex gives 👍/no-suggestions; leave exact blocker summary if blocked.
   - If pi is already running, read its herdr pane tail and agent status. If it is idle/done but has not pushed/requested fresh Codex review and there is no blocker, nudge it to continue from the current state with the same requirements. Do not hand-edit the repo. If it reports a blocker, verify enough of the blocker via pane output/GitHub state and report succinctly.
4. Monitor existing pi sessions: use herdr workspace/pane list/read. Pane IDs can change; resolve by label/worktree path from state before acting. Do not trust stale IDs blindly. Do not broad-kill or clean up processes. Do not use rm -rf.
5. After pi pushes a new head, update state with the new head sha and request/await a fresh Codex review. Repeat on later ticks until current-head Codex approval/no-suggestions.
6. Keep output quiet-by-default: if nothing changed and no blocker/completion, final response should be a one-line quiet status or empty-ish brief. If you launched/nudged a session, requested review, found feedback, saw completion, or hit a blocker, report the PR number, action, pane/worktree, and next watch condition.

Safety/authority boundaries:
- Aaron explicitly authorized PR feedback remediation for this repo, but Hermes must remain supervisor-only. Use pi inside herdr for code changes.
- Preserve unrelated local changes. Do not reset/discard force-push unless pi has explicit, evidence-backed reason and it is scoped to that PR branch.
- Do not merge PRs unless Aaron separately asks. The success condition here is Codex 👍/no-suggestions and updated PRs.
- Use official GitHub/Git/herdr/pi outputs as evidence. Never invent tool results.
